title: Baseline and deviation detection
description: Normal behavior is baselined per identity and per endpoint: typical request rates, hours, and volumes. Live activity is compared to the baseline with z-scores; deviations beyond threshold flag for review. Baselines adapt slowly so gradual legitimate change does not false-alarm. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers per-identity and per-endpoint baselines.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: 12, 2: 45, 3: 200}
obs, mean, sd = CFG[LEVEL], 10.0, 2.0
z = (obs - mean) / sd
print("observed %d vs baseline %.0f±%.0f: z=%.1f" % (obs, mean, sd, z), "->", "FLAG" if abs(z) > 3 else "normal")
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Impossible-travel detection
description: Logins from geographically distant locations within an impossible time window indicate credential compromise or sharing. The detector computes required travel speed between successive logins and flags the physically impossible. VPN and travel exceptions are handled via declared itineraries. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers travel-speed computation between logins.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: (100, 2), 2: (8000, 1), 3: (500, 5)}
km, hours = CFG[LEVEL]
speed = km / hours
print("login moved %d km in %dh = %.0f km/h" % (km, hours, speed), "->", "IMPOSSIBLE-TRAVEL FLAG" if speed > 1000 else "plausible")
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Burst detection
description: Sudden spikes in request volume versus recent history indicate scraping, brute force, or runaway clients. The detector compares short-window counts against longer baselines and flags multiplicative jumps. Bursts trigger rate limiting first and investigation second. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers short-window vs baseline comparison.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: (100, 110), 2: (100, 500), 3: (100, 5000)}
baseline, now = CFG[LEVEL]
ratio = now / baseline
print("baseline %d -> now %d (x%.1f)" % (baseline, now, ratio), "->", "BURST: rate-limit" if ratio > 5 else "normal")
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Known-abuse pattern matching
description: Attack signatures (credential stuffing rhythms, enumeration sequences, scanner fingerprints) are matched against live traffic. Pattern libraries come from incident history and threat sharing. Matches fire with the pattern name and recommended response attached. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers attack-signature libraries.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: ["login-ok"], 2: ["login-fail"] * 20 + ["login-ok"], 3: ["/admin", "/wp-admin", "/.env"]}
events = CFG[LEVEL]
stuffing = events.count("login-fail") >= 10
scanning = sum(1 for e in events if e.startswith("/")) >= 3
print("events:", len(events), "| credential-stuffing:", stuffing, "| scanner:", scanning)
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Risk scoring and triage
description: Signals combine into a composite risk score: anomaly size, pattern matches, asset sensitivity, and identity history. Scores map to actions: allow, challenge (step-up), or block. Triage queues are ordered by score so analysts work the riskiest first. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers composite scores from multiple signals.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: 15, 2: 55, 3: 92}
score = CFG[LEVEL]
action = "allow" if score < 30 else ("challenge" if score < 70 else "BLOCK")
print("risk score:", score, "->", action)
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.
